glance_takeaway: This is an architecture map of 'meridian', a self-hosted read-later/RSS service with ~13,710 lines of backend Python. The core message is that data flows one way: an ingest pipeline (scheduler -> queue -> fetcher -> extractor -> dedup) writes into a single SQLite file owned solely by store/, and an HTTP API, a vanilla-JS web reader, and a CLI read it back out. It also flags hotspots -- extractor.py is the biggest/riskiest file, there is exactly one layering violation, the web reader has no tests -- and tells a newcomer their first change goes in pipeline/sources/ or api/routes.py, never store/ or queue/.

F1.note: All six packages appear as boxes (pipeline/, queue/, store/, api/, render/, cli/) plus 'web/ -- vanilla-JS reader ... no framework, no build step'.

F2.note: Top-row arrows scheduler -> queue -> fetcher -> extractor -> dedup -> store; store box: 'triggers keep the FTS index in sync'. Caption 2: 'schedule -> fetch -> extract -> dedup -> store'. Queue insertion is consistent extra detail, not a reordering.

F3.note: 'writer.py . 610 LOC -- ALL writes live here', 'reader.py ... reads -> frozen dataclasses', rule 1 'only store/writer.py writes the DB'.

F4.note: 'extractor.py -- pure ... no network . disk . DB . clock'; rule 2 'extractor is pure -- a property test replays 1,400 fixture pages in CI'.

F5.note: Red callout: 'extractor.py line 41 imports clean_html() from render/sanitize -- a sideways pipeline -> render edge (since v0.8) ... issue #214'.

F6.note: 'layering: store/ imports nothing; nothing imports api/ or cli/' in the rules box.

F7.note: '1,140 LOC -- largest file in the repo . 14 site heuristics' on the extractor box.

F8.note: Subtitle '13,710 lines of backend Python'; header 'pipeline/ ... 4,180 LOC ... largest module'.

F9.note: Footer strip 'backend 13,710 LOC at 77% line coverage . frontend 0%'; store 91% cov, cli/ 41% cov, web/ '0 automated tests -- no JS harness at all'.

F10.note: '412 tests -- 348 unit + 64 integration . ~41 s' bottom strip.

F11.note: dedup.py box: '64-bit simhash . Hamming <= 3 => dup . ~7% of items dropped'.

F12.note: 'add a source type -- the 4-file recipe' lists sources/base.py, sources/__init__.py, store/migrations/, cli/commands/add.py exactly.

F13.note: queue/ box: 'no broker . jobs table in SQLite . 8 workers . depth 30-60 . alert @ 500'; amber note 'jobs table = a table in the same SQLite file'.

F14.note: 'GET /articles/{id} -- p50 28 ms (store 6 + template 14 + annotations 8)' with green store->render->api arrows.

F15.note: 'schema.sql -- 9 tables + articles_fts (FTS5)' and 'triggers keep the FTS index in sync -- Python never writes it'; rule 3 'the index can never drift'.

render_issues: None functionally. Minor: the red warning text '1,140 LOC -- largest file in the repo' runs to the very edge of the extractor's red outline; a few dashed wires cross other edges in the mid-canvas, adding slight visual noise. No-JS fallback (static final frame + ordered caption list) and prefers-reduced-motion are handled correctly.
strengths: Perfect fact audit: all 15 ground-truth facts are present and numerically exact, including the negative facts (layering violation, 0% frontend tests, 41% cli coverage) which are given prominent red treatment rather than sanded off.

The above-the-fold frame carries all four critical takeaways at once: headline/subtitle state the shape, red outlines mark the hotspot, the rules box states the invariants, and a bold bottom caption states exactly where first changes go.

Color legend is bound to meaning (write path / store hub / read path / caution) and used consistently across boxes, arrows, and annotations, so the one-way flow is readable without tracing every edge.
weaknesses: Wayfinding within one large SVG canvas is weaker than sectioned prose: there are no headings to scan or anchor to, so re-finding a specific number means visually re-scanning the whole diagram; the step dots help only if the reader discovers the JS controls.

Very high text density at small (12-12.5 px) sizes above the fold; a 10-second glance yields the headline takeaways but the mid-canvas annotations (e.g. the amber jobs-table note, the p50 dequeue label) compete for attention.

The build-up animation is the approach's namesake feature but is invisible in the default final-frame state; a reader who never presses 'replay the build-up' gets no benefit from the 7-step narrative captions.
